sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Manish Kumar Vijaywargiya - Advocate for the app  Shri Tarun Pagare - P.L. for respondent/State.
 Shri Ram Lal Patidar, learned counsel for the Objecto  ORDER 1.
Heard and perused the record.
2. This is the first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail.

The applicant is arrested in connection with Crime No.8/2023,
registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, Mandsaur, District Mandsaur for the offence under Sections 354(A), 509(B), 294, 506, 376-D, 292 of IPC and 67(a), 66-D of Information Technology Act.
The applicant is in jail since 26/11/2023.
3 . As per prosecution, on 9/8/2023 a complaint has been lodged by the prosecutrix stating that co-accused Ajay Mevad liked her photo on instagram and started messaging her continuously.
Thereafter he started blackmailing her and also made a video calls and asked her to remove her clothes and recorded the same in his mobile and thereafter viral her videos.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31840 2 MCRC-41844-2024 4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that at initial stage these allegations were not mentioned in the FIR against the present applicant - Amarpal Malviya whereas the name of main Amarpal Malviya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183189867/
1 accused Ajay Mevad has been mentioned.

sentences.text: However, later on the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 and 164 of the Cr.P.C whereby the name of the present applicant has been added in the FIR on 12/10/2023, after two months of the alleged incident.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the alleged incident.
He is in jail since 26/11/2023 and has completed approximately one year in custody.
Certainly the present prosecutrix has made allegation in her Court statements under Section 161 and 164 but they are belatedly and after thought.
On such grounds, prayer for grant of bail to the applicant has been made.

5 . The aforesaid prayer is opposed by counsel for the respondent/State as well as by learned counsel for the Objector submitting that the application for grant of bail of the main accused has recently been dismissed by this Court on 23/9/2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.35834 of 2024 on the basis of the statement of the prosecutrix before the trial Court.
The name of the present applicant has also been mentioned in her statement hence in view of the allegations levelled against the applicant, he is not entitled to be released on bail.
6 . I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the case diary as well as the record.

7 . Considering all the aspects of the case and also the fact that the name of the present applicant has been added after two months in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31840 3 MCRC-41844-2024 investigation proceedings and also considering the period of custody of the applicant, this Court is inclined to grant the bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application filed by the applicant is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/ - with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the Court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
8 .
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE SS/-
